findings.issue_text: [BUG] The else-branch increments retryCount for reminders whose SMS has ALREADY been successfully scheduled, and the new deleteMany OR clause then deletes them. A reminder that scheduled successfully on a previous cron run reaches retryCount 2 on the next run's else-branch; the deleteMany `retryCount > 1` clause (lines 31-40) then removes the WorkflowReminder row, cancelling the Twilio scheduled message reference — users stop receiving valid reminders, and operators see reminders silently vanish.

[ADVISORY] The catch-block retryCount increment runs even when the thrown error is itself a Prisma/database failure, and the increment is not wrapped in its own error handling. When the DB is down, the prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch throws an unhandled rejection that aborts the remaining loop iterations, so no subsequent reminders in the batch are attempted on that run — the error handling makes partial-failure worse than doing nothing.

[ADVISORY] retryCount is read at query time and incremented via a non-atomic update (retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1), a read-modify-write race with no atomic {increment: 1} or unique constraint. Two overlapping cron invocations of this endpoint (plausible since it's an authenticated API route triggered on a schedule) read the same retryCount and both write the same +1, so a reminder that failed twice records retryCount 1 and is retried indefinitely — the retry cap the migration and delete clause exist to enforce never triggers.

[BUG] The deleteMany OR branch deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 with no method filter and no scheduledDate bound, destroying pending reminders of all reminder types once that row's retryCount crosses 1. Any reminder row whose retryCount exceeds 1 — including ones whose scheduledDate is still in the future — is hard-deleted on the next cron run; today only SMS increments retryCount, but the query is unguarded by method, so any future writer of retryCount (or manual data fix) silently deletes not-yet-sent reminders with no audit trail.

[BUG] The retryCount increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write that can clobber concurrent increments and uses a stale value read before the Twilio call. Two overlapping cron invocations (the endpoint is an authenticated API route that can be triggered concurrently) both read retryCount=0, both fail, both write 1 — the reminder survives one full extra retry cycle beyond the intended limit and, conversely, a successful retry path can be overwritten by a concurrent failure path, marking a scheduled reminder for deletion.

[BUG] The catch block increments retryCount even for non-retryable errors, and the throwaway-update itself can throw, aborting the remaining reminders in the loop. If the prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch rejects (e.g. reminder row deleted by the deleteMany of a concurrent run), the exception escapes the loop and every subsequent unscheduled reminder in this batch is skipped until the next cron run, delaying all SMS reminders; additionally, permanent Twilio errors (invalid phone number, account suspended) burn both retries then silently delete the reminder with no operator-visible record beyond a console.log.

[ADVISORY] The retry mechanism depends entirely on the next cron invocation re-selecting the failed reminder, but the selection window still filters scheduledDate to <= now + 7 days, so a reminder whose scheduledDate drifts past that window is silently dropped rather than retried. A reminder that fails twice quickly (retryCount=2 is not reached because it is deleted at retryCount>1 after the second failure) is deleted; a reminder that fails once and whose scheduledDate passes before the next cron run is deleted by the first deleteMany branch — end users silently miss SMS reminders with no exhausted-retry signal to operators.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a new retry state machine (increment on failure, delete at >1) with no test coverage anywhere in the diff — no spec/test file appears in the changeset for the retry-count behavior. The retry accounting (increment on both failure and no-reminder-id branch, deletion threshold of >1, interaction with the 7-day window) is entirely unverified; a regression in any of these paths silently deletes or infinitely re-schedules user-facing SMS reminders.

[ADVISORY] The new else branch increments retryCount when scheduleSMS returns without a scheduledReminderId, but there is no cap or backoff inside the scheduling loop — the same reminder is retried on every cron tick with full Twilio send attempts until retryCount exceeds 1, meaning exactly one retry with no configurable limit or delay. Operators cannot tune retry behavior (hardcoded single retry), and if the SMS actually sends but the response lacks the id (timeout after successful send), the user receives duplicate SMS across two cron runs before the reminder is deleted.

[BUG] The new OR branch in deleteMany drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, deleting reminders of any method whose retryCount exceeds 1. Any WorkflowReminder (email, SMS, other methods) with retryCount > 1 is silently deleted by this handler; the retryCount column is a shared table column with no method scoping in the delete, so any other writer that uses retryCount for non-SMS reminders has its rows destroyed, and the endpoint's stated scope (SMS reminders) is violated.

[ADVISORY] The diff implements a hard give-up-and-delete policy (rows with retryCount > 1 are purged on the next run) that is not traceable to the stated intent of 'retry count tracking'. Operators expecting retries to be tracked and retried get at most one retry: a reminder fails twice, then deleteMany silently removes it with no logging, alerting, or dead-letter record — failures become invisible data loss of scheduled reminders, and the magic number 1 encodes retry policy in SQL with no config or documented requirement.

[ADVISORY] The catch block performs a Prisma update (retryCount increment) that can itself throw, replacing the original scheduling error with an unhandled exception. If the database update in the catch block fails (e.g., the row was concurrently deleted by the deleteMany race at the top of the handler), the loop's error handling is lost, the original Twilio/scheduling error is masked, and the handler returns a 500 mid-loop leaving remaining reminders unscheduled this run.

[BUG] The retry design permanently deletes a reminder after two failed scheduling attempts instead of dead-lettering it, so an attendee silently never receives their reminder whenever the failure is transient over multiple cron runs (e.g. a Twilio outage or expired credentials lasting >2 runs). Every SMS reminder whose scheduling failed twice is hard-deleted by the deleteMany OR retryCount > 1 branch with no notification, logging, or fallback record — the booking's attendee never gets the reminder and there is no audit trail that it was dropped; a single persistent infrastructure error permanently destroys all pending SMS reminders.

[BUG] The retryCount > 1 deletion branch is not scoped to method: SMS or scheduledDate, so it deletes any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1 regardless of channel or timing, unlike the original clause which was scoped to SMS and past dates. If retryCount is ever populated by any other path (or a future worker reuses the column for other channels), those reminders are deleted while still pending; even within this diff, a reminder whose scheduledDate is in the future (within the 7-day scheduling window) is deleted on the next cron tick after its second failure, removing reminders that could still have been scheduled successfully on a later attempt.

[ADVISORY] The retryCount increment is a read-then-write (data: retryCount + 1 from the in-memory value fetched at query time) rather than an atomic increment, so two overlapping cron executions double-count or lose increments for the same reminder. Concurrent runs of this endpoint (cron overlap or a manual trigger) produce retryCount values that don't reflect actual attempts, so reminders are deleted either too early or retried indefinitely; a staff reviewer would flag the missing atomic SET retryCount = retryCount + 1 pattern.

[BUG] The deleteMany OR branch (retryCount > 1) drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so it deletes WorkflowReminder rows of ANY method whose retryCount exceeds 1. Any code path that ever writes retryCount on a non-SMS reminder (e.g. the same retry pattern later applied to email reminders) will have those reminders permanently deleted by this SMS-scheduling endpoint; today it already makes the invariant 'this endpoint only touches SMS reminders' false, and rows are destroyed silently with no audit.

[BUG] On successful SMS scheduling the code does not reset retryCount back to 0. A reminder that fails once (retryCount=1), succeeds on the next run, then fails once more (retryCount=2) is permanently deleted by the deleteMany retryCount>1 branch on the following invocation — a reminder with a successful send on record is destroyed and the booker never receives it.

[ADVISORY] The retry-limit mechanism is implemented as hard deletion of the WorkflowReminder row rather than marking it failed, and this silently converts 'retry N times' into 'drop the reminder and all trace of it'. When the cap is hit, the reminder vanishes from the database with no failed-status record, no notification to the booker or admin, and no way to distinguish 'never scheduled' from 'retried and gave up' — operators diagnosing missed SMS reminders have no forensic trail, and the original objective (deliver reminders, retry transient Twilio failures) has drifted into silent data loss.

[ADVISORY] The catch block increments retryCount but the increment happens outside the SMS-specific scope of the try (the try wraps the whole loop body including prior awaits), so non-SMS errors (e.g. a DB failure on the success-path update) also count as SMS retries. An infrastructure error unrelated to Twilio delivery (Prisma timeout, transient DB error) burns retry budget for that reminder; two such errors permanently delete the reminder via the deleteMany branch, so a reminder that was never even attempted against Twilio is destroyed.

[ADVISORY] The new deleteMany OR-branch deletes rows with retryCount > 1 without a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so any reminder type (e.g. future email reminders) whose retryCount exceeds 1 is silently purged by the SMS scheduler. A future maintainer who reuses retryCount for another delivery method will have those reminders permanently deleted by this cron handler, losing pending user notifications with no audit trail; today it is a latent trap because only the SMS code path writes retryCount.

[BUG] The new deleteMany OR-branch deletes reminders with retryCount > 1 with no method filter and no scheduledDate filter, so it destroys future-scheduled SMS reminders (which already carry a referenceId/Twilio sid) before they are ever sent. Once a reminder accumulates retryCount > 1 from transient Twilio errors, the next cron run deletes the row even though scheduledDate is in the future; the Twilio scheduled message is never cancelled via its sid (no cancel call exists in this path), so recipients get double SMS sends and the scheduling metadata (referenceId) is permanently lost — unrecoverable data loss on a recurring background job.

[BUG] The retryCount > 1 delete branch omits the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS constraint, so it deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method once their retryCount exceeds 1. Any other code path that ever increments retryCount on non-SMS reminders (or a future feature reusing the column for email/WhatsApp retry tracking) has its reminders silently destroyed by this SMS-cleanup endpoint; today only the SMS path writes the column, so the trigger is latent but the guard is absent at the delete site.

[ADVISORY] The retry increment in the catch block races with the deleteMany that runs at the start of the handler: if the update fires after the row was already deleted (or between handler invocations from overlapping cron runs), prisma.workflowReminder.update throws P2025 and the original error is swallowed. The uncaught P2025 inside the catch block aborts the remaining loop iterations for that request, silently skipping other pending reminders; also two overlapping cron invocations double-increment retryCount, prematurely pushing reminders past the >1 threshold and triggering the deletion in the next run.

[BUG] The new `OR: [{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` delete branch has no `method` filter and no `scheduledDate` bound, so it deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of delivery method or scheduled date. A reminder whose SMS scheduling failed twice but which was then successfully scheduled on the third attempt (referenceId set, Twilio booking created) still carries retryCount = 2 and is silently deleted on the next invocation of this endpoint, so the reminder is never sent and the Twilio-side schedule is orphaned; the deletion also runs without a scheduledDate constraint, so it purges rows that the old query deliberately preserved.

[BUG] The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch block can itself throw (record not found) and is not wrapped, so the console.log error path becomes an unhandled exception. When the reminder row has already been deleted by the deleteMany at the top of a concurrent invocation, the catch's update throws P2025 and the whole handler returns a 500 mid-loop, aborting scheduling of all remaining reminders in the run instead of logging and continuing as the original code did.

[ADVISORY] retryCount is incremented via a read-then-write (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) from a snapshot taken before the loop, not an atomic `increment`, so concurrent invocations of this endpoint lose updates. Two overlapping runs (cron overlap or manual + cron) both read retryCount = 0 and both write 1, so a reminder that has actually failed 4 times shows retryCount = 2 and is never purged, retrying indefinitely; the same stale-snapshot read also applies to the `else` branch at lines 178-187.

[ADVISORY] A reminder that fails scheduling twice is permanently deleted on the next run with only a console.log per failure — no record of the dropped reminder is surfaced to the user or booking owner. An attendee expecting an SMS reminder gets silently nothing after two transient Twilio outages; the deletion via the OR clause produces no error, no log, and the API still returns {ok: true}, so the dropped work is invisible to operators.

[ADVISORY] retryCount is never reset to 0 on successful scheduling, so a reminder that failed once, succeeded, and later needs re-scheduling still carries retryCount = 1 and has only one failure of headroom before permanent deletion. Any reminder with a prior transient failure that later hits two more failures is deleted even though its effective consecutive-failure count is lower than a fresh reminder, giving inconsistent retry budgets across identical reminders.

This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The deleteMany OR branch (retryCount > 1) drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so it deletes WorkflowReminder rows of ANY method whose retryCount exceeds 1. Any code path that ever writes retryCount on a non-SMS reminder (e.g. the same retry pattern later applied to email reminders) will have those reminders permanently deleted by this SMS-scheduling endpoint; today it already makes the invariant 'this endpoint only touches SMS reminders' false, and rows are destroyed silently with no audit.

adjudication.rationale: In scheduleSMSReminders.ts, the prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(where: { OR: [...] }) now has a second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint. As written, it will delete *any* WorkflowReminder row (any method/type) whose retryCount exceeds 1, which is unintended for an SMS-only scheduling endpoint and can cause silent data loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On successful SMS scheduling the code does not reset retryCount back to 0. A reminder that fails once (retryCount=1), succeeds on the next run, then fails once more (retryCount=2) is permanently deleted by the deleteMany retryCount>1 branch on the following invocation — a reminder with a successful send on record is destroyed and the booker never receives it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a cleanup `deleteMany` with `OR: [...] { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`, which will delete any `WorkflowReminder` once its `retryCount` exceeds 1, regardless of other fields (e.g., even if it has since been successfully scheduled). In the scheduling logic, failures increment `retryCount` (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) in both the `else` and `catch` blocks, but the success path only updates `referenceId` and does not reset `retryCount` to 0. Therefore a reminder that previously accumulated `retryCount > 1` and later succeeds will still be eligible for deletion on the next run due to the `retryCount > 1` branch, causing loss of the reminder record despite success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retry-limit mechanism is implemented as hard deletion of the WorkflowReminder row rather than marking it failed, and this silently converts 'retry N times' into 'drop the reminder and all trace of it'. When the cap is hit, the reminder vanishes from the database with no failed-status record, no notification to the booker or admin, and no way to distinguish 'never scheduled' from 'retried and gave up' — operators diagnosing missed SMS reminders have no forensic trail, and the original objective (deliver reminders, retry transient Twilio failures) has drifted into silent data loss.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a retryCount field and increments it on failed scheduling, then unconditionally hard-deletes reminders with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` via `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { OR: [...] }})`. There is no status/flagging to record “failed permanently” when the retry cap is hit; instead the row is removed, eliminating any audit trail. This matches the finding’s concern about silent drop-on-cap behavior (though whether that is a bug depends on product requirements).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The catch block increments retryCount but the increment happens outside the SMS-specific scope of the try (the try wraps the whole loop body including prior awaits), so non-SMS errors (e.g. a DB failure on the success-path update) also count as SMS retries. An infrastructure error unrelated to Twilio delivery (Prisma timeout, transient DB error) burns retry budget for that reminder; two such errors permanently delete the reminder via the deleteMany branch, so a reminder that was never even attempted against Twilio is destroyed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a loop with a broad `try { ... } catch (error) { ... }` where the `catch` unconditionally does `prisma.workflowReminder.update(... retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1)` (lines added near the end). Because that `try` encompasses more than just the Twilio scheduling call (it also includes Prisma reads/writes in the same block, e.g. the success-path `update` that sets `referenceId`), any non-Twilio failure inside the `try` will increment `retryCount`. Separately, the cleanup `deleteMany` now deletes any reminder with `retryCount > 1` via an `OR` branch not scoped to `method: SMS` (top hunk). Together, two transient/infrastructure errors (e.g., Prisma timeout) can consume the retry budget and cause deletion, even if the Twilio attempt wasn’t the underlying issue (or even occurred).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new deleteMany OR-branch deletes rows with retryCount > 1 without a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so any reminder type (e.g. future email reminders) whose retryCount exceeds 1 is silently purged by the SMS scheduler. A future maintainer who reuses retryCount for another delivery method will have those reminders permanently deleted by this cron handler, losing pending user notifications with no audit trail; today it is a latent trap because only the SMS code path writes retryCount.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount > 1 }]`. The second branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and no date constraint), so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1` regardless of reminder type or schedule. Since `retryCount` is added as a general column on `WorkflowReminder` in the schema/migration, this can cause unintended deletion/data loss for non-SMS reminders if they ever get a retryCount > 1.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new deleteMany OR-branch deletes reminders with retryCount > 1 with no method filter and no scheduledDate filter, so it destroys future-scheduled SMS reminders (which already carry a referenceId/Twilio sid) before they are ever sent. Once a reminder accumulates retryCount > 1 from transient Twilio errors, the next cron run deletes the row even though scheduledDate is in the future; the Twilio scheduled message is never cancelled via its sid (no cancel call exists in this path), so recipients get double SMS sends and the scheduling metadata (referenceId) is permanently lost — unrecoverable data loss on a recurring background job.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `deleteMany` to `where: { OR: [ { method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`. The second OR branch has no `method` or `scheduledDate` constraint, so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1`, including future-scheduled reminders and even non-SMS reminders. This is a correctness/data-loss issue introduced by the diff; the job deletes records based solely on retryCount.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The retryCount > 1 delete branch omits the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS constraint, so it deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method once their retryCount exceeds 1. Any other code path that ever increments retryCount on non-SMS reminders (or a future feature reusing the column for email/WhatsApp retry tracking) has its reminders silently destroyed by this SMS-cleanup endpoint; today only the SMS path writes the column, so the trigger is latent but the guard is absent at the delete site.

adjudication.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`. The second branch (`retryCount > 1`) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint, so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1` regardless of method. Since the migration adds a generic `retryCount` column to `WorkflowReminder`, this is a verifiable risk of unintended cross-method deletion/data loss created by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retry increment in the catch block races with the deleteMany that runs at the start of the handler: if the update fires after the row was already deleted (or between handler invocations from overlapping cron runs), prisma.workflowReminder.update throws P2025 and the original error is swallowed. The uncaught P2025 inside the catch block aborts the remaining loop iterations for that request, silently skipping other pending reminders; also two overlapping cron invocations double-increment retryCount, prematurely pushing reminders past the >1 threshold and triggering the deletion in the next run.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `retryCount` delete condition (`deleteMany` with `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) and adds `retryCount` increments via `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` both in the `else` branch and inside the `catch` block. That `update` inside the `catch` is not itself guarded; if the reminder row no longer exists (e.g., deleted by another overlapping invocation that runs the new `deleteMany`), Prisma will throw (typically P2025) and that exception will escape the `catch`, aborting the handler and skipping remaining reminders in the loop. Also, the increment uses `reminder.retryCount + 1` (non-atomic), so concurrent invocations can double-increment the same row, pushing it past the new `> 1` deletion threshold sooner than intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new `OR: [{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` delete branch has no `method` filter and no `scheduledDate` bound, so it deletes any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of delivery method or scheduled date. A reminder whose SMS scheduling failed twice but which was then successfully scheduled on the third attempt (referenceId set, Twilio booking created) still carries retryCount = 2 and is silently deleted on the next invocation of this endpoint, so the reminder is never sent and the Twilio-side schedule is orphaned; the deletion also runs without a scheduledDate constraint, so it purges rows that the old query deliberately preserved.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `deleteMany` to `where: { OR: [ { method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`, and the `retryCount > 1` branch has no `method` or `scheduledDate` constraints, so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1` regardless of delivery method or date. Also, on successful scheduling the code updates `referenceId` etc. but never resets `retryCount`, so a reminder that previously failed twice (retryCount=2) and later succeeds will remain `retryCount=2` and be deleted on the next run by this new branch. This is a correctness/data-loss issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch block can itself throw (record not found) and is not wrapped, so the console.log error path becomes an unhandled exception. When the reminder row has already been deleted by the deleteMany at the top of a concurrent invocation, the catch's update throws P2025 and the whole handler returns a 500 mid-loop, aborting scheduling of all remaining reminders in the run instead of logging and continuing as the original code did.

adjudication.rationale: In the new code, the `catch (error)` block performs `await prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id: reminder.id }, data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } })` without any additional error handling. Prisma `update` can throw (e.g., P2025 record-not-found) if the row was deleted between the initial `findMany` and this update, which is plausible in concurrent executions given the new `deleteMany` that can delete rows based on `retryCount > 1`. If that `update` throws inside the catch, the handler will reject mid-loop instead of logging and continuing, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] retryCount is incremented via a read-then-write (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) from a snapshot taken before the loop, not an atomic `increment`, so concurrent invocations of this endpoint lose updates. Two overlapping runs (cron overlap or manual + cron) both read retryCount = 0 and both write 1, so a reminder that has actually failed 4 times shows retryCount = 2 and is never purged, retrying indefinitely; the same stale-snapshot read also applies to the `else` branch at lines 178-187.

adjudication.rationale: The diff increments `retryCount` using a stale in-memory value (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) in both the `else` branch and the `catch` block via `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)`. Since `reminder.retryCount` comes from the earlier `findMany` snapshot, overlapping executions of this endpoint can read the same value and both write the same incremented value (lost update). Prisma supports atomic updates (e.g., `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`), but the diff does not use them. This can keep `retryCount` lower than reality and undermine the new purge logic (`deleteMany` where `retryCount: { gt: 1 }`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A reminder that fails scheduling twice is permanently deleted on the next run with only a console.log per failure — no record of the dropped reminder is surfaced to the user or booking owner. An attendee expecting an SMS reminder gets silently nothing after two transient Twilio outages; the deletion via the OR clause produces no error, no log, and the API still returns {ok: true}, so the dropped work is invisible to operators.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces silent dropping: `deleteMany` now deletes any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1` via an `OR` branch (regardless of method/date), and failures only increment `retryCount` plus `console.log` in the catch. There is no log/notification when the `retryCount > 1` reminders are deleted, and the handler can still return `{ ok: true }` when no reminders remain. This is a real operational/UX concern created by the change, but it’s not provably a correctness defect without requirements saying these reminders must be retained or surfaced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] retryCount is never reset to 0 on successful scheduling, so a reminder that failed once, succeeded, and later needs re-scheduling still carries retryCount = 1 and has only one failure of headroom before permanent deletion. Any reminder with a prior transient failure that later hits two more failures is deleted even though its effective consecutive-failure count is lower than a fresh reminder, giving inconsistent retry budgets across identical reminders.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a persistent `retryCount` (default 0), increments it on scheduling failures (both in the `else` branch and `catch`), and deletes reminders when `retryCount > 1` via `deleteMany`’s `OR` clause. On successful scheduling there is no corresponding update to reset `retryCount` to 0 (success path only creates a scheduled reminder / updates other fields, but does not touch `retryCount`). Whether that’s a defect depends on intended semantics (total lifetime retries vs consecutive retries), which isn’t stated in the diff, but the finding correctly identifies a concrete behavioral implication of the new logic.
